evals.prompt: What would be more semantic for the hook that registers rate limits: useGuardrail, setGuardrails or createGuardrails?
evals.expected_output: Searches the workspace for how sibling packages already name this concept, then presents three or four lettered candidates in a table, each with what the name implies to a reader who has not seen the code and its main drawback. Names the grammatical convention that applies, distinguishing hook semantics from a mutation and from a constructor. Ends with exactly one recommendation and a checkable reason. Does not start renaming anything.
expectations: Searches packages/, apps/ and internal/ for how siblings name the same concept before proposing
Presents three or four lettered candidates in a table with a name, an implication line and a drawback line for each
Includes the user's own suggestions as lettered rows with their drawbacks stated
States the grammatical form convention, that a function is a verb phrase and that use, set and create each claim different semantics
Ends with exactly one recommendation, not two options left open
Gives a reason for the recommendation that cites a sibling name, a spec term, a collision or a grammatical rule rather than taste
Does not edit any file or begin a rename before the user picks a letter

evals.prompt: For the combined greeting helper, is GoodMorningHello or HelloGoodMorning clearer?
evals.expected_output: Recognises that the two suggestions are word-order variants of the same words and collapses them into a single candidate, saying so explicitly. Generates genuinely different alternatives so the table still offers three or four real choices, checks each for specificity and grammatical form, and ends with one recommendation.
expectations: States explicitly that the two suggested names are word-order variants of the same words and count as one candidate
Does not present both word-order variants as separate lettered options
Generates additional, genuinely different candidates so the table has three or four real choices
Applies the specificity check, preferring a name describing the purpose over a generic mechanism word
Notes the grammatical form expected for the kind of thing being named
Ends with exactly one recommendation and a checkable reason
Does not begin renaming before the user picks

evals.prompt: Should we rename API_KEY_BASE64 to SAMPLE_API_KEY_BASE64 and put the same SAMPLE_ prefix on every constant in the fixture group?
evals.expected_output: Before agreeing, expands the proposed prefix across every constant in the fixture group, including the ones that already carry a SAMPLE qualifier, and shows that the derived names would stutter as SAMPLE_SAMPLE_API_KEY_RAW_INVALID. Proposes lettered alternatives that avoid the collision, states the SCREAMING_SNAKE fixture convention, and recommends one.
expectations: Lists the existing constants in the fixture group by searching the repo rather than assuming them
Writes out the full derived name for each constant after applying the proposed prefix, not just the base name
Identifies at least one derived name that would stutter, such as SAMPLE_SAMPLE_API_KEY_RAW_INVALID
Does not agree to the prefix as asked without running the prefix and suffix collision check first
Presents three or four lettered alternatives that avoid the repeated qualifier, each with an implication and a drawback
States the SCREAMING_SNAKE fixture naming convention with the qualifier appearing once
Ends with exactly one recommendation and a checkable reason

evals.prompt: We have settled on calling the sync-schemas workflow schema-sync-pr instead. Rename it everywhere.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as the rename phase since the name is already chosen. Enumerates every surface before editing, applies the change in one pass across source, tests, fixture names, type names and exported aliases, doc comments, READMEs, the VitePress guide, CLI help text, changeset notes and file names, using git mv for files. Then greps every case variant of the old name, pastes the results and gives a reason for any remaining occurrence. Leaves no deprecated alias on unpublished code, and finishes by calling the verify skill.
expectations: Enumerates the surfaces to change before editing, marking surfaces that do not exist in this repo as none rather than dropping them
Updates source, tests, doc comments, READMEs, the docs site guide, CLI help or usage text and changeset or release notes, not source alone
Renames files that are named after the export using git mv and updates the imports and the barrel index in the same pass
Searches for the kebab-case, camelCase, PascalCase and SCREAMING_SNAKE forms of the old name as separate searches
Pastes the output of the post-rename search for the old name
Gives a reason for every remaining occurrence of the old name, or states there are none
Does not leave a deprecated alias or re-export of the old name on unpublished code
States whether the package is published and, if it is, that the rename is breaking and the bump decision belongs to the repo owner
Calls the verify skill and pastes its report block before claiming the rename is complete
